digest.component_or_area: Backend port exception contract (Jira reconciler transport)
propositions: The Backend port declares no exception contract, so core reconciler modules catch the transport-specific urllib.error.HTTPError, a Cloud-specific leak in vendor-neutral code.
The DC transport raises jira.exceptions.JIRAError, which core catch clauses do not match, so a set_reporter 4xx escapes instead of degrading softly.
On DC, a remotely-deleted issue is not classified as _DELETED because JIRAError matches neither the HTTPError nor URLError branches in _safe_get_issue, silently breaking deletion detection.
BackendHTTPError is declared on the port subclassing urllib.error.HTTPError and carrying .code, so existing core catch sites work unchanged and Cloud is not touched.
The DC transport translates JIRAError into BackendHTTPError at the adapter boundary, preserving the HTTP status code, so a DC 404 classifies as _DELETED like Cloud.
A DC non-404 (403/500/503) must map to _TRANSPORT_ERROR not _DELETED, and no JIRAError should appear in any core module.
